name: Live in Virginia Beach
description: Recorded in Virginia Beach, Virginia on the 2001–2002 Midnight Drivers / Across The World Tour and released in February 2003 following Crimson Node and Live at the Chancellery. Having road-tested a mysterious unnamed new song for a few weeks on tour, The Stardust Engine tests whether the hometown Virginia Beach crowd knows the words mid-concert—marking the first time 'The Flight Path' was ever recorded for a future live album while fans still believed it was simply a new Stardust Engine track.
subtitle: The 2001–2002 Across The World Tour — First Recorded Live Album Performance of "The Flight Path" (Mid-Concert Placement)
linerNotes: Before the world met Crimson Node during the May 2002 encore at The Chancellery in Charlottesville—and before Crimson Node's self-titled debut studio album finally revealed the song's title on September 18, 2002—The Stardust Engine had spent several weeks quietly road-testing a mysterious, unnamed new anthem in the middle of their concerts.

Recorded in the O'Connell and Wright family's original hometown during the 2001–2002 Across The World Tour, Live in Virginia Beach is the earliest live performance of 'The Flight Path' ever captured for a live album. Slotted right in the middle of the set at Track 08 without a title announcement or any mention of another band, Ryan and Cassidy challenged the Virginia Beach crowd to see if they already knew the words from the past few weeks of tour tape-trading—and 20,000 fans roared every line of the chorus right back at the stage, still completely convinced it was a brand-new Stardust Engine song. Released in November 2002 as the fifth and final step of the 2002 Crimson Node rollout, the album opens with 'The Stardust Engine' and closes with 'Electric Color'.

studioArchives.title: Testing the Virginia Beach Crowd (Mid-Concert Singalong)
studioArchives.content: Because The Stardust Engine had been road-testing the mystery song for the past few weeks on tour, hardcore Forger Nation tape-traders had already learned the lyrics by the time the tour rolled into Virginia Beach. When Ryan and Cassidy launched into Track 08 to see if Virginia Beach knew the words, the entire amphitheater sang along—even though not a single fan in the venue knew the name of the song or that it wasn't a Stardust Engine song!

studioArchives.title: The Five-Step 2002 Chronology
studioArchives.content: (1) Live in Virginia Beach (the concert) happens first, featuring 'The Flight Path' in the middle of the set (with the crowd already singing along after a few weeks of road-testing, though no song name is given—marking the first time the song is recorded for a future live album). (2) Live at the Chancellery (the concert at The University of the Piedmont's indoor arena in Charlottesville) happens in May 2002, where Crimson Node is introduced after 'Electric Color' to close the concert, and Holly O'Connell works with Crimson Node to get the studio version of 'The Flight Path' onto FM radio. (3) Crimson Node (the studio album) debuts on September 18, 2002, giving fans the name of the song. (4) Live at the Chancellery (the album) is released in October 2002. (5) Live in Virginia Beach (the album) is released in November 2002.

studioArchives.title: Sacred Setlist Boundaries
studioArchives.content: Following The Stardust Engine's canonical live architecture, the concert opens with 'The Stardust Engine' and closes with 'Electric Color', while 'If You Walked Away' remains permanently retired out of respect for Cassidy's autistic boundaries.
